claim: The damage layer has two rules for a roofless wing's roof bays. §2.6 step 7 (l.2085–2086) calls the threshold test "the one comparison every reader makes": an element is damaged when the level reaches its t, otherwise not. V03 §5.6 (2) (c) (l.2697–2702) and V02 §5.7 (2) (l.3064–3066; X34, T-V2-59 (b)) also mark every roof bay over a room of a roofless wing (`RoofSpec.kind 'none'`: the decline's `decayed` and `ruined` states, a fire's `charred` shell) as damaged, whatever its threshold. That is what keeps the inside and the outside in agreement (item 123 (d)): V06 §3.23 (2) starts a `decayed` building at level 1/3, and V11's `roofBay` range is 0.40–0.66 (l.4596). So a newly roofless building has no roof over it on the exterior, while under §2.6's one comparison every roof bay in its plan stays intact. The rule is shared by two volumes but stated only in them, and the base's home denies it.
required_change: §2.6 step 7, after the comparison sentence: "One case has no threshold: while a building is `decayed` or `ruined` — in a decay run, or read at V11's default age with no run in the log (V06 §3.23 (4)) — every roof bay over a room of a wing whose `RoofSpec.kind` is `none` (the decline's roofless state, a fire's charred shell) is damaged whatever its t, so the plan's open ceilings are the roof the exterior lacks (item 123 (d)); nesting holds, the state only climbing while the run lasts; a standing wing an author roofed `none` keeps its plan unchanged. V03 §5.6 (2) (c) and V02 §5.7 (2) cite this." Rendering writes §8.6's end in the same round (VAF-R2T-02; R2-05).

claim: §2.6 step 7 says each element is shown damaged "whose t it has reached (level ≥ t), the one comparison every reader makes", with t in [0, 1). Three other units word it differently: §6.3 *Plan damage* (the threshold's home), V03 §5.6 (2) (a) and V11 §3.25.10 all say "the level above 0 and at least t". V11 admits lo = 0: `0 ≤ lo < hi ≤ 1`, and a range moves freely inside its states' shares, with `abandoned` at [0, 1/3]. A draw u = 0 is lawful. So under "level ≥ t" a never-decayed building (level 0) can show an element damaged. That breaks item 123 (f)'s no-op bar (`item123.damage`), which the same paragraph states. The set states "the one comparison" in two forms.
required_change: §2.6 step 7: "shows damaged every element whose t it has reached (level ≥ t), the one comparison every reader makes" → "shows damaged every element whose t it has reached (the level above 0 and at least t, §6.3 — so a level of 0 damages nothing), the one comparison every reader makes".

claim: A raised way laid BEFORE an enceinte trace that later crosses it (walls × raised ways; opened by round 2's crossing station; not in the catalogue; distinct from peer VM-R2T-03, the band's decay under a station). §2.7's crossing station (support step (3), base l.2528–2536) is laid only when the support step runs — 'after its course and deck level are fixed and before the span rule' (l.2512–2513) — and no text re-runs it when a trace or moat is later laid across a standing raised way. At generation: a viaduct is raised 'inside S4's route solve (and each later stage's S5b through this router)' (§4.3 The slot, l.5590–5591), before every later stage's trace; S5b makes the existing arterials' crossings of the new boundary its gates (l.5769–5776), so a stage-k+1 gate falls on the deck; S5a's Outer moats (l.5754–5765) carve the channel, put a fresh part-0 deck on 'the arterial just outside each gate' and state 'Nothing finer than L1 exists yet, so the carve's footprint clears nothing' although the viaduct's pier footprints stand on ground part 0; §4.8 S7 lays no raised gate (only V06's epoch rule names one). At an epoch: V06 §3.7.6 (5) crosses a standing aqueduct or viaduct 'only under a span over land, never through a support' (V06 l.1570–1571), i.e. between stations, while J-V6.140 and the same item call the opening 'the deck's station on the trace … its pier the wall's band' (l.1582–1583, l.4385); V06 §3.7.1 widens t_k until every existing footprint is at least the strip's width + growth.ringBlockM from the boundary (l.1435–1437) and §3.7.6 (5) counts the raised way's supports as footprints, which at the masonry pitch of 8–15 m (V11 l.3942) against an 18–33 m strip (§4.8 l.7469–7472) no boundary across the raised way can satisfy. As written the earlier stations stand: piers left in the new ring's setback, glacis, berm and moat channel (the carve clears nothing; §5.3 has no invariant on a support in water), no station on the trace, the clear-span bound never re-read — a silent wrong result against §2.7's 'no support in water' and T110-2's '0 piers in a setback, glacis, berm or moat'; at an epoch an unsatisfiable widening (T-V6-47 expects the crossing under a span). T110-2's crossing fixtures (l.17988–17992) cover only a course laid after the wall it crosses.
required_change: §2.7's support step: add '(6) A trace or moat laid across a standing raised way — a later stage's S5a trace and outer moat at generation, an epoch's circuit, contraction or re-anchored stretch (V06 §3.7.6 (5)), a hand drawWall — re-runs (1)–(5) on that raised way in the same commit: the crossing station on the new trace (the nearest interior station within p ÷ 2 moved there, keeping its key, else one added), the stations in the new strip's setback, glacis, berm or channel slid or omitted by (3); where a clear span on either side of the station would then pass maxClearSpanM, or a pier maxPierM, the trace gives way (S5a: its stage trace takes the next lattice boundary node off that span, reported; V06: retrace and wait, walls.waited) — a standing raised way is never dropped for a wall.' Other ends this round (R2-05): §4.4 S5a Outer moats (pipeline) — 'the carve clears no raised-way support: (6) re-sites one first in the same commit; a stage gate on a raised arterial is a raised gate whose tower carries the deck, the deck itself crossing the channel (no part-0 deck added for it), the part-0 way beneath taking its own ground gate'; §4.8 S7 (pipeline) — the raised gate and the aqueduct's wall opening as generation furniture in V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s form; V06 §3.7.1 (V06) — its footprint-distance test excepts the supports of a raised way the trace crosses, within one strip width of the crossing; §13.2 T110-2 (scope) — a CITY c14 fixture whose S4 viaduct over a valley is crossed at a gate by stage 2's moated ring, and an epoch circuit across a standing aqueduct: each crossing's one station on the trace, 0 piers in a setback, glacis, berm or moat, the raised way kept.

claim: G123's new §2.6 step 7 says the plan in force stands — 'the stored plan, else the one re-derived from its canonical prior at the building's built band and era (the as-built plan, below …)'. V03 §3.11 *Decay re-cuts no plan* (b) (J-V3.137), the volume that builds and draws the plan, re-derives an unstored plan 'at the occupant inputs it held in the week before its run began … the plan the building was last lived in, which for a building never re-let is its as-built plan'. They differ for every building re-let or re-banded before it was left: under §2.6 the plan a user saw is replaced at abandonment by the as-built layout — 'redrawn as new', against item 123's owner words and §2.6's own 'the plan in force stands'. And §2.8's elaboration record (the home of the plan rung's inputs and stale triggers) still lists the households housed, the occupants' band and value and 'its running Works' stage' as inputs and stale triggers with no decay-run exception, while V03 §3.11 and V03's lifecycle row (l. 302: 'no stale mark, §2.8') say the leaving stales nothing and a `decay` or `repair` Works is no build stage — V03 cites a §2.8 rule §2.8 does not state.
required_change: (1) §2.6 step 7: replace '— the plan in force stands, the stored plan, else the one re-derived from its canonical prior at the building's built band and era (the as-built plan, below; V03 §3.11's vacant re-cut is a standing building's only) —' with '— the plan in force when its decay run began (V06 §3.23 (1)) stands: the stored plan, else the one re-derived from its canonical prior at the occupant inputs it held in the week before that run began (V03 §3.11 *Decay re-cuts no plan*: the plan it was last lived in, its as-built plan (below) when never re-let); V03 §3.11's vacant re-cut is a standing building's only —'. (2) §2.8, `ElaborationRecord.inputs`, the plan rung: 'its running Works' stage at the drawn week (item 67 (j))' → 'its running build Works' stage at the drawn week (item 67 (j); a `decay` or `repair` Works is none, §2.6 step 7)'; and in the `stale` sentence, after 'a dossier event of items 18, 22 or 31;', add 'for a building in a decay run (V06 §3.23 (1)) its occupant inputs — use, assignment, sub-locations, concealed use, the households housed and the occupants' band and value — are those of the week before its run began (V03 §3.11), so neither the leaving nor a later move of the field stales its plan;'.

claim: §2.6 step 7 restates the decay level and its comparison (R2-38 (3)–(4)'s summary words) against their homes. Level: §2.6 reads it 'from its existence state, the years since the week of the epoch whose op set it `abandoned`' and gives V11's default age to 'a building with no abandonment epoch (generated ruined; first met in item 113's replay)'; V06 §3.23 (1)–(4), the level's home (R2-38 (3)), starts the decay run at the effective week (V06 §2.11) of the lifecycle event that took the building from a standing state into `abandoned`, `decayed` or `ruined` — a `vacate`, a fire's `burn`, a flood's or a topple's `ruin` — and keeps the default age for a building with no decay run in the log. So a building a fire burns or a flood ruins, or one a hand edit abandons between epochs, ages from that week in V06 but sits at the default age under §2.6. Comparison: §2.6 calls 'level ≥ t' 'the one comparison every reader makes', while §6.3 *Plan damage* (the thresholds' home) shows an element damaged 'exactly while the level is above 0 and at least t — a level of 0 damages nothing'; V11's ranges admit lo = 0 (T-V11-47), so an element can draw t = 0 and §2.6's comparison damages it on a standing building, against §2.6's own 'a building never decayed (level 0) draws byte-identically' (`item123.damage`).
required_change: §2.6 step 7: replace 'the building's **decay level** — V06's `decayLevel(doc, lineage, week)` in [0, 1], derived and never stored, from its existence state, the years since the week of the epoch whose op set it `abandoned` (its lifecycle events, §2.8) and V11's rate by material (timber faster than stone), read at the drawn week (§2.9's `week`) — shows damaged every element whose t it has reached (level ≥ t), the one comparison every reader makes.' with 'the building's **decay level** — V06 §3.23's `decayLevel(doc, lineage, week)` in [0, 1], derived and never stored, from its decay run (from the effective week, V06 §2.11, of the lifecycle event that took it from a standing state into `abandoned`, `decayed` or `ruined` — a `vacate`, a `burn`, a `ruin`; its lifecycle events, §2.8), its state and V11's rate by material (timber faster than stone), read at the drawn week (§2.9's `week`) — shows damaged every element whose t it has reached while above 0 (level > 0 and level ≥ t; §6.3 *Plan damage*), the one comparison every reader makes.'; and 'A building with no abandonment epoch (generated ruined; first met in item 113's replay)' → 'A building with no decay run in the log (generated abandoned, decayed or ruined; first met so in item 113's replay; V06 §3.23 (4))'.

claim: The round-2 support step (3) (VEW-r1-03, R2-26 (c)) makes the wall's band the support where a course crosses an enceinte: 'the wall carries the deck there — a … raised gate, whose tower carries the deck, or the curtain under an aqueduct's arch … that station's support `ring` is the band's stretch under the deck, the wall's own masonry (no pier raised …)'. That stretch stays on the enceinte's condition profile, which item 114's writers break: V06 §3.7.7 (2) breaches stretches in chain order (neglect, poverty, both low) and `DeclineOp`'s `breach` names any stretch; V06 §3.7.6 (5) holds the stretch only against V06 §3.7.2 (2)'s dismantling while the deck stands (a landfall is defined: V05's table breaches the wall and ruins the span and support it covers). No text says what a decay breach of the band under a standing deck does — the deck keeps a station whose support is 'a gap with rubble', or its spans merge across it past the clear-span bound; neither the support step, the span rule, V06 §3.7.7 nor V06 §3.19 defines it, and no bar covers it (T110-2 builds the crossing; the item-114 group decays rings with no raised way). Principle (11): walls decaying into gaps × a raised way carried by the wall, opened by this round's crossing station.
required_change: §2.7's support step (3), after 'the clear-span bound reads the spans on either side of that station (T110-2)', add: '; while the deck stands, the stretch of the band under a crossing station is held by it — `DeclineOp`'s `breach` and V06 §3.7.7 (2)'s decay pass over it in chain order as V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s dismantling does (it may wear, and a repair writes it as any run), a landfall over it breaching it and ruining the deck there by V05's landfall table — and from the first epoch after the raised way is removed or the spans on either side fall it is an ordinary run'; V06 §3.7.7 (2) cites it (V06's end); §13.2's item-114 group gains the fixture (scope's end): a neglected, poor CITY ring over 20 epochs with a masonry aqueduct through its wall arch and a viaduct on a raised gate — the stretch under each crossing station never `breached` or `dismantled` while its deck stands, every other stretch decaying as T114-1 states.

claim: G122h's §2.9 *The crisis framing* says 'Only the opening view, Fit and the limit change'. §9.5's *Framing* circle is both the initial view and the default export frame, and §9.5 widens that circle while a look stands; §8.7 cuts every export frame to the bounds of town and camps. So the default export frame changes too, which §2.9's 'only' denies.
required_change: §2.9 *The crisis framing*: 'the opening view (§9.5's *Framing* circle, widened to contain every camp, and with it the default export frame that circle sets; every export frame cut to those bounds, §8.7)', and 'Only these framings change: a view the user has moved is never re-framed (item 122 (i))'.

claim: §2.7's *Readers* line restates V06 §3.7.7 (3): 'patches rebuilt oldest first by the week of each run's `conditionEpoch` — its `EpochRecord.week`, so a replay epoch's patch before every live one's (§6.1) —, ties in chain order'. A run patched at generation carries `conditionEpoch` 0, which has no `EpochRecord`; V06 §3.7.7 (3) states 'generation's epoch 0 first', §2.7's restatement does not, so read alone it leaves the oldest case undefined.
required_change: §2.7, *Readers*: 'volume 6's transitions (V06 §3.7.7 (3): patches rebuilt oldest first by the week of each run's `conditionEpoch` — generation's epoch 0 first, a replay epoch's before every live one's (§6.1) —, ties in chain order)'.

claim: Whether the surrounding ring's massed camp marks widen item 116's limit is stated two ways. §8.8 *The surrounding ring* (and T-ER-08: 'the ring's arcs among them') says the arcs 'count among the camps the crisis framing takes in (§2.9), so the limit shows them'; §2.9 *The crisis framing* defines the bounds of town and camps as 'the union of `bounds` … and every camp the looks place, §10.2's placement inside the frame and its margin', the ring (outside the margin) only 'drawn as §8.8's massed marks', and §10.2 (g) speaks of 'the placed camps' bounds'. Read by §2.9, the city-band ring may lie outside the view at the limit.
required_change: §2.9's *The crisis framing* parenthesis reads '(the union of `bounds`, …, every camp the looks place — §10.2's placement inside the frame and its margin — and the ring's massed camp marks beyond it, §8.8's *The surrounding ring*)'; §10.2 (g)'s 'The placed camps' bounds' reads 'The placed camps' and the ring arcs' bounds' (pipeline's end).
